item.use: Mostly heard as kaze fuiteru with a describing word: ii kaze fuiteru (there's a nice breeze), tsumetai kaze fuiteru (a cold wind's blowing). For 'it's windy', people say kaze ga tsuyoi.
item.verbSense: blow (wind; also blowing air from your mouth)
item.trap: kaze is both 'wind' and 'a cold', and only the verb tells you which: kaze ga fuku is the wind blowing, kaze o hiku is catching a cold.

examplePolite.ja: いい風が吹いてますね。

item.freqNote: Kana ふく is dominated by 服 and 拭く, so the kanji 吹く is used.
item.notes: kaze ga yamu = the wind dies down.

set: kaze ga dete kita = the wind's picking up. For no wind at all people say kaze ga nai.
base.why: kaze ga fuku was cut in review as guessable; restored because the learner asked for it by name ('wind blows') and the wind/cold homophone is a real listening trap.

final.why: restore: the other half of opposite or ga/o pairs whose partner was kept; all five judged common (4/5) but rare in foreign-film subtitles.
